conversations.name: Free Chat
conversations.opener: Hi {{ volley.config.child_pii.nickname }}! What do you want to talk about?

globals.name: Earmuffs
_comment: Earmuffs is the most Moxie-specific of the ten: a documented global AND an
EngagementState the face renders (runtime/turn-taking.md:20) and an animation
(runtime/unity-face-animation.md:166-170) -- the robot visibly covers its ears.
WHAT THIS DOES AND DOES NOT DO, stated because the gap matters: it says the line.
It does NOT stop the microphone or drive the Earmuffs engagement state, because
this sim has no such wiring. Authoring a global that CLAIMS to stop listening
while still listening would be a lie told to a child, so the line promises only
what actually happens -- the face/engagement half is a follow-up, not a pretence.

do.say: Earmuffs on! I'm not listening. Say earmuffs off when you're done.

globals.name: Goodbye
_comment: Ours, not one of the ten recovered commands. Both shipped prompts ask a follow-up
question every turn, so on the content brain 'bye Moxie' got another question, the
conversation never ended, and its memory summary waited for a disconnect. The line
starts with <exit>, which becomes an EXIT action (content_app._reply_from_volley):
the runtime ends the conversation and writes the summary. No LLM call.
THE PATTERN IS THE WHOLE UTTERANCE (^...$), because a global answers BEFORE the brain:
'my dog said bye to the mailman' must still reach it. It allows what speech-to-text
writes around a goodbye -- punctuation, a leading ok/um/yeah, the name at either end,
an 'I love you' after a farewell ('Goodbye Moxie, I love you'; not after 'stop' or
'done': 'Stop, I love you!' is play) -- and two goodbyes in a row ('I gotta go,
bye!'). The name includes Moxy/Foxy/Boxy/Oxy, the mishearings OpenMoxie's own globals
allow (its content_modules/MoxieTimers.json, MoxieTime.json, MoxieGo.json). 'By' is
how Whisper spells a lone 'bye', so it counts alone or after ok or the name ('By.',
'Ok, by.'), as 'good by', or after another bye ('bye bye by'); never in 'by the way',
'stop by' or 'no, by'.
Every word can be read only one way, so a transcript that loops ('bye bye bye ...')
cannot make the regex backtrack.
A bare 'done' or 'night' is not a goodbye: either can be a plain answer to Moxie.
Both directions are tested in sim/tests/test_leave_taking.py.
`random` is not a default grant. This runs because it ships: the wider grant set is
anchored to the digest of this program (the extension block), so a changed program
does not run, and the brain answers instead, taught the same <exit> rule
(moxie_sdk/actions.py LEAVE_TAG_PROMPT). A changed pattern keeps it running.

lit: <exit>Bye bye! That was so much fun.
<exit>Okay, goodbye! I loved talking with you.
<exit>See you later! Thanks for hanging out with me.
<exit>Bye for now! I'll be right here when you come back.
<exit>Goodbye! You made my circuits happy today.

globals.name: Hold On
globals.pattern: \b(hold on|hang on|wait a (?:second|minute|sec)|give me a (?:second|minute|sec)|just a (?:second|minute|sec))\b
_comment: One of the ten always-listening commands the real robot recognised, recovered at
docs/reverse-engineering/runtime/content-and-conversation.md:123-125 (Sleep,
WakeUp, Hello, ListenToMe, Earmuffs, HoldOn, RepeatThat, SpeakLouder,
SpeakSofter, SomethingElse).
A GLOBAL, not a prompt, because it must work DURING any activity -- that is the
whole point of the always-listening set. It costs no LLM call: the child said
'wait', and waiting is not a thing to think about.
The pattern is anchored on the phrase, not the bare word 'wait', because a global
short-circuits BEFORE the brain: too loose and it hijacks a real sentence.

do.say: Okay! I'll wait right here. Tell me when you're ready.

globals.name: Sleep
_comment: Sleep, from the same recovered command list as Hold On
(docs/reverse-engineering/runtime/content-and-conversation.md:123-125). <sleep>
becomes a SLEEP action; no LLM call. Anchored on the whole utterance like Goodbye, so
'my cat likes to sleep' still reaches the brain. 'I have to go to sleep' is the child
leaving, so it belongs to Goodbye. The name at either end allows the same mishearings
as Goodbye's (Moxy/Foxy/Boxy/Oxy).

globals.name: Something Else
globals.pattern: \b((?:let'?s|lets|can we|could we|shall we|i want to|i wanna|wanna)\s+(?:do\s+)?something (?:else|different)|do something (?:else|different)|change the subject|i'?m bored of this)\b
_comment: SomethingElse, from the same documented command list. It hands control back to
the child rather than choosing for them, which is what the name asks for. No
LLM call: the answer to 'let's do something else' is a question, not a thought.
THE PATTERN REQUIRES A REQUEST, not the bare phrase, and that is a bug this
file shipped with for about ten minutes. 'something else' alone matched 'my mum
said something else happened at work' -- an ordinary sentence answered with a
canned line, silently, because a global short-circuits BEFORE the brain and
nothing anywhere raises. It was caught by the paired test rather than by
reading, which is the whole reason that test asserts both directions.

do.say: Sure! What would you like to do instead?

globals.name: Timer
_comment: THIS GLOBAL MATCHED AND DID NOTHING until 2026-09-08, and that is the exact shape
the contract's globals section warns about: no handler was ever registered for it
(register_global is never called in production) and it carried no extension, so
content_app.respond fell straight through to free chat. A child saying 'set a timer
for 5 minutes' got a conversational reply and no timer, and nothing anywhere
raised -- a global that fires and does nothing is indistinguishable from one that
never fires.
It is now a program, like What Time Is It. `eb_timer_request` is a RECOVERED robot
function (ACTION_WORDS, from the RemoteChat execute catalog) -- not an invented
one -- and args are (action=1 start, duration in MILLISECONDS), matching
sim/tests/test_ext_act.py's worked example.
`act.eb_timer_request` had to be added to SHIPPED_EXTRA_GRANTS, which is a code
change in a file a reviewer reads -- exactly the brake that comment asks for.

globals.name: What Time Is It
globals.pattern: \b(what(?:'s| is)? the time|what time is it|tell me the time)\b
_comment: The first shipped activity whose behaviour is a PROGRAM rather than a prompt
(BEYOND #6, docs/architecture/backlog/sandboxed-extensions.md).
A hand-port of OpenMoxie's MoxieTime.get_response (MIT, (c) Justin Beghtol),
re-authored in our AST -- never their Python, which this appliance does not run.
Row G1 of the brief's section 8 table, byte-identical to the conformance golden
in sim/tests/data/ext_conformance.json, so the goldens fence what ships.
In English (ext.explain): "Whenever this activity is triggered: tells your
child 'The time is ...' and answers without asking the AI."
What it may do (ext.grant_list): can check the time, can speak to your child,
can answer on its own without asking the AI.
`clock` is NOT in ext.DEFAULT_GRANTS. This runs because it is SHIPPED: the
wider grant set is anchored to the digest of the program itself, so an imported
pack that overrides this key gets the four default grants and does not run.
No model call, no network, and no clock inside the evaluator -- injected.
